newsitem.title: UK: UK shares end down, near day's lows as Dow weakens.
newsitem.headline: UK shares end down, near day's lows as Dow weakens.

text.p: UK shares dropped on Friday as a fresh bout of jitters hit Wall Street and gilts dropped sharply amid profit-taking and political worries after a local election defeat for the ruling Conservative party.
The FTSE 100 index closed 30.9 points lower at 4,308.3, having earlier bounced off the 4,300 support level. Losers were in a seven-to-two majority,

With concern already growing over next Friday's U.S. jobs report, traders said there were fears that this week's warning of overvalued shares from Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan could be preparing the ground for a rise in interest rates.
The Dow was down about 40 points as London closed while U.S. Treasury bonds were little changed despite a downward revision of fourth quarter U.S. economic growth.
"The market here has been a bit spooked by Wall Street," said one senior trader.

"Greenspan seems to be paving the way for an interest rate rise at some point, maybe as early as next month," the trader added. "Despite the lower fourth quarter GDP, people are saying he has an interest rate rise in mind and has been tempering the damage which may be done."
Dealers said the FTSE 100 should suffer less than the Dow in any correction, having underperformed on the way up, but said shares here remained vulnerable to any sharp fall in U.S. markets.
"It has been a long bull run over there and we are probably long overdue a correction," one said.

Trading volume in London reached a moderate 764.2 million by 1656 GMT, with the FTSE 250 index of second-line stocks also falling but by less than the blue chip FTSE 100. The 250 ended down just 8.6 points at 4,654.4. The Reuters-HSBC index of the leading 150 UK stocks fell 8.07, or 0.7 percent, to 1,162.35.
On the week, the FTSE 100 fell 28.5 points, having hit a near-record 4,357.9 on Tuesday.
News of the Conservative party's defeat in the Wirral South by-election did little to cheer sentiment, helping send the March long gilt future down 3/4 to 112-15/32 by the close of business.
However, traders said a defeat for the ruling party in the national election due by the end of May should already be priced into stocks.
They said continued weakness in the Dow were more to blame for London's performance, still unsettled by Fed chief Greenspan's warning against "excessive optimism" on Wall Street.

Still, traders said a continuing flow of institutional cash into equities should limit any downside for markets, with no imminent threat to the steady growth, low inflation environment in which stocks have advanced in recent months.
"There isn't a lot of stock around in this market and there is still a lot of cash coming in, so I don't feel we will go down any great distance," one said.
Standard Chartered was the biggest gainer in the FTSE 100, up 27p or 3.3 percent at 842-1/2 as Lehman Brothers raised the stock to "buy" and buying continued after Wednesday's results.
HSBC Holdings, also heavily involved in Asian markets, was up 17-1/2p at 15.80-1-/2 ahead of results on Monday.
In the same sector Abbey National fell 13-1/2p to 754-1/2 following negative press and broker comment in the wake of the group's annual results.
Zeneca Group fell 33-1/2p to 18/05 stg after the company said it had received a warning from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration over its manufacturing facilities in the UK.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
